The class of cyclic codes is an important class of linear codes which has been extensively studied over ﬁnite
rings after the establishing work of Hammons et al. [ 7] in 1994. Like commutative rings [ 9, 11–14],
noncommutative rings also play an important role in the development of error-correcting codes. Apart from
skew polynomial rings [ 4, 8, 10], rings of matrices have recently attracted a growing interest among
researchers. In 2012, Oggier et al. [ 16] considered the matrix ring M
2ðF2Þ for space-time coding. In 2013,
Alahmadi et al. [ 1] studied cyclic codes over M2ðF2Þ and explored certain self-dual F4-codes. Also, in 2014,
Falcunit and Sison [ 5] investigated the structure of cyclic codes over M2ðFpÞ by using an isometry between
M2ðFpÞ and Fp2 þ uFp2 . Recently, Luo and Udaya [ 15] considered the matrix ring M2ðF2 þ uF2Þ and
obtained several optimal F4-codes of length 16 and 20, respectively as the Gray images of cyclic codes.

1. Introduction
Cyclic codes over finite rings have been at the centre of attraction 
among researchers since 1994 [9]. They have a rich algebraic structure and, 
consequently, produce a huge amount of good linear codes. Initially, cyclic 
codes were considered over finite commutative as well as noncommutative 
rings. To discover new codes, cyclic codes over finite commutative rings 
are investigated in [7, 10–12, 14–17, 19, 22, 24, 25, 29]. Till now, a few papers 
[1, 3, 5, 8, 13, 18, 20, 21, 23] have come into the literature that presented the 
study of these codes over noncommutative rings, namely, matrix rings.

Construction of Codes Over Fp3 From Cyclic Codes
Over M3(Fp + uFp + u2Fp)
Shikha Patel1, Soham Ravikant Joshi 2 and Om Prakash 3
1Department of Mathematics, Indian Institute of Information Technology Bhopal, Bhopal- 462 003, India

Abstract—Let Fp be a finite field with p elements and
Fp[u]/⟨u3⟩ = Fp + uFp + u2Fp, u3 = 0 be a finite chain ring.
This paper presents the construction of cyclic codes over Fp3 for
certain primes (p ≤ 100) from a noncommutative non-chain ring
R = M3(Fp[u]/⟨u3⟩) of 3 × 3 matrices. First, we show that the
structure of R is isomorphic to (Fp3 +eFp3 +e2Fp3 +u(Fp3 +eFp3 +
e2Fp3)+u2(Fp3 +eFp3 +e2Fp3) where e3 = 1, u3 = 0, uiej = ejui
for i ∈ {1, 2} and j ∈ {1, 2, 3}. Then we provide the form of ideals
of R and derive that cyclic codes can be written as the direct sum
of R-submodules of R[x]
<xn−1> . Further, we find the formula for the
cardinality of cyclic codes over R. Later, in the module isometry
for R, we define the Gray map, which takes derived cyclic codes
over R to Fp3. In addition, we provide non-trivial examples of
linear codes over Fp3 with good parameters which support our
derived results.
Index Terms—Finite field, cyclic codes, matrix rings, Gray map,
MDS/AMDS codes.

Abstract
Let Fp be the ﬁnite ﬁeld with p elements where p is a prime, and R b ea3 ×3 matrices
over Fp[u]/⟨uk ⟩, i.e., R = M3(Fp + uFp +···+ uk−1Fp) with uk = 0. First, we
study the structure of cyclic codes over R as the direct sum of submodules of R, along
with the Euclidean and Hermitian dual for the ring S = M3(F3 +uF3 +···+ uk−1F3).
Later, to show that the structure is suitable for the construction of good linear codes,
we provide many AMDS (almost maximum-distance-separable) and best-known lin-
ear codes over F125, F27, and F8. Further, we study dual-containing codes over S
using a new non-degenerate inner product and provide a new approach to constructing
quantum codes over matrix rings via the CSS (Calderbank-Shor-Steane) construction.
Finally, we construct several quantum codes with small quantum Singleton defects
using a suitable Gray map.

Quantum codes
